content.thinking:
I need to avoid writing any actual digits or figures myself, using placeholders instead for things like durations, timestamps, and counts, while spelling out small numbers in words like "both versions" rather than numerals.

Working through the causal chain: users saw account page failures with error rates spiking between {began} and {recovered}, caused by replicas failing to read a composite cache entry that the deployment had switched to from a simpler format. I'm tracing this to a stalled rollout where replicas were split between old and new revisions sharing a cache, with old parsers unable to read the new composite entries—rolling back to the prior revision confirmed this as the root cause, though the split-rollout detail rests on the Investigator's assumption.

Contributing factors include no staged compatibility check for the format change and a detection gap, since the alert fired several minutes after errors actually began. I'm drafting new action items: a tolerant reader or two-phase format rollout, alerting on stalled rollouts or cache parse errors, and a pre-deploy review step for shared-state format changes—noting that rollback did eventually resolve things once triggered.

action_items.item: Make the summary cache reader accept both the bare cents format and the composite format. Roll the change out in two phases: first deploy the tolerant reader everywhere, then deploy the writer that emits the new format.

Alert on a rollout that stays split between revisions beyond a set time, and on a rise in summary cache parse errors, so a stalled mixed-version state is flagged before the general error-rate alert fires.

Add a pre-deploy review check and a test that runs the previous revision's reader against the new revision's writer. It should be required for any change to the format of shared cache or storage entries.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average between {began} and {recovered}, peaking at {errors_at_worst}, and the account page error warnings climbed with it.
The failing requests raised a ValueError because a summary cache entry was not a figure in cents. The service was reading a composite 'amount/items' value where it expected a bare integer.

The deployment at {began} changed the summary cache entry format from a bare cents integer to a composite 'amount_cents/items_counted' string. The first parse errors appear at the same time as that deploy.

The rollout did not converge. Replicas on the old revision and replicas on the new revision were live against the same shared cache at once. Old-revision code still parses entries as a bare integer, so it fails on entries the new revision wrote. The break existed only while both versions were running together.

The new format was shipped as a direct replacement, not as a change the old reader could tolerate. Nothing before or during the rollout caught that the old and new revisions could not read each other's cache entries. Rolling back removed the mixed state, and the error rate returned to baseline.

contributing_factors.factor: A change to the format of shared state (the summary cache) went out as a single-step replacement. The old revision's reader could not handle the new format, and no review or test checked compatibility between adjacent revisions during a rollout.
The stalled, split rollout was not flagged. Cache parse errors were reaching shoppers until the general error-rate alert paged at {alert_raised}, after the onset at {began}.

input.executive_summary: For about {duration}, from {began} to {recovered}, a share of shoppers' account page requests failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. A software release changed how a small piece of shared cached data was stored. For a while, servers running the old release and servers running the new release were both live. The old ones could not read what the new ones wrote. Argus rolled the release back, the error rate returned to baseline, and Argus confirmed recovery and closed its response after {held}. A draft fix has been proposed for review.

got_lucky: The failure was limited to the account page summary and the mixed-version state was reversible. A rollback was enough, with no cache cleanup shown as needed in the record.
went_well: Argus read metrics, logs and change events, and identified the format change as the leading cause within seconds of being called in.
The rollback was applied quickly. Argus confirmed the metrics returned to baseline and the paging rule stopped firing, and the response was held for {held}.
A draft fix was proposed as a pull request right after mitigation.
went_wrong: A cache format change that was not backward compatible reached production and stalled the rollout in a mixed-version state.
The alert fired at {alert_raised}, after the onset at {began}, so shoppers were failing before anyone was paged.

input.root_cause: The deployment at {began} changed the format of entries in the shared summary cache from a bare cents figure to a composite string. The rollout stalled with old and new revisions live together, so old-revision replicas could not parse entries written by new-revision replicas, and account page requests failed.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
